# Atmosphere Processors
[italic]"Remarkable piece of machinery, completely automated. You know, we manufacture those, by the way."[/italic]
An [bold]Atmosphere Processing Plant[/bold] (APP), usually just called an [bold]atmosphere processor[/bold] or "atmos", is a huge automated reactor that turns a toxic or unbreathable atmosphere into air humans can breathe. They are the backbone of colonization: without one, most worlds can only be settled under domes or underground.
## History - Weyland Corp pioneered the technology. Its first processor was switched on on Earth in 2016 and effectively ended global warming. - In 2039, GJ-667Cc became the first planet given a breathable atmosphere by one. - Weyland-Yutani still builds them on the same basic chemistry Weyland patented over a century ago, and sells them along with matching pressurizers that bring a world's air pressure up to Earth-like levels. - Not every power has them. The [textlink="Union of Progressive Peoples" link="CMUGuideLoreUPP"] and [textlink="Seegson" link="CMUGuideLoreCorporations"] never developed their own, which is why they build under domes, underground or in orbit instead.
## How It Works - A processor is a cone-shaped tower around 1,500 meters tall, built around a fusion reactor. - It draws in the native atmosphere through vents in its base and sides, compresses it with turbines, and heats it to near-plasma temperatures until its molecules break apart into single atoms. - Magnetic fields then sort the atoms by element. Hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen are released from the top of the tower as breathable air, while carbon and other leftovers are collected as fuel, solvents or raw materials. - Engineered mosses, grasses and flowering plants are often seeded alongside it to help turn carbon dioxide into oxygen. - The process takes decades. Once the air is stable, the processor keeps monitoring it and corrects any imbalance on its own.
## Colonies - The conversion is automatic, but a processor still needs a permanent crew to maintain it, and many colonies exist mainly to run one. - If its critical systems are badly damaged, the reactor can melt down in an enormous explosion that can wipe out everything around it. - Atmospheric reactors are vital infrastructure. Attacking one is a Crime Against Humanity under [bold]Article 29[/bold] of the [textlink="Geneva Conventions" link="AU14UCMJGENCON"], unless the planet's civilians have been evacuated and a hostile force is using it as a combat position.
